name: mcp-surgeon
stderr:
mcp-surgeon — lint your MCP server

Usage:
  mcp-surgeon lint [--call] [--header 'Name: Value']... -- <command> [args...]
  mcp-surgeon lint [--call] [--header 'Name: Value']... -- <https url>

Options:
  --call            also invoke each tool once (minimal args derived from
                    its schema) and lint the live responses. Opt-in: calls
                    can have side effects on a real server.
  --read-only       like --call, but only invoke tools that are safe to
                    call (readOnlyHint, else a read-only name); skip the
                    rest. Implies --call.
  --args-file <f>   JSON file mapping tool name -> real probe arguments,
                    e.g. {"get_page":{"page_id":"<real id>"}}. Listed
                    tools are called with YOUR data (hits the happy path);
                    unlisted tools keep schema-derived placeholders.
  --init-args-file <f>  write that file for you: every advertised tool
                    mapped to the placeholder args the probe would use.
                    Edit in real values, re-run with --args-file <f>.
                    Refuses to overwrite an existing file.
  --header 'K: V'   extra request header for an HTTP target (repeatable),
                    e.g. --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. For an
                    HTTP target, MCP_AUTH_TOKEN (from env or .env) is sent
                    as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' automatically.
  --insecure        skip TLS certificate verification for an HTTP target.
                    INSECURE — only for testing self-signed servers.

Examples:
  mcp-surgeon lint -- node dist/index.js
  mcp-surgeon lint --call -- npx -y some-mcp-server
  mcp-surgeon lint --read-only -- https://host/mcp
  mcp-surgeon lint --header 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -- https://host/mcp
